could_not_do: RI-UIX09 DN4 / RULING S56 — THE PANEL SIZING IS NOT BUILT. This was the 'if you have room' item and I did not have room; I am reporting it undone rather than half-done, because a half-done version breaks six screens. WHAT I ESTABLISHED BY READING RATHER THAN GUESSING: the panel is ONE constant, `BOX = { x: 200, y: 160, w: 1520, h: 780 }` at `game/src/ui/chrome.js:70`, consumed by `screenRect()` and therefore by every screen through `screen()`. So 'size the panel to its contents' is not one edit to one constant — it is a per-screen box plus a rewrite of each screen's vertical layout, because every screen positions against `sc.inner` in ABSOLUTE offsets that assume the current height. Two measured examples: `screens/inventory.js` puts the worn band at `iy + 476*s`, the sort control at `iy + 574*s` and gold at `iy + ih - 40*s`, so any height below ~614 units collides; `screens/progress.js` `drawSheet` runs 8 fact rows at 34 units and 10 attribute rows at 42 units (272 and 420 units) while the skills column is written to FILL `ih`, so the sheet's contents height is circular until the skills window is re-derived. THE ARITHMETIC ALSO DOES NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH THE INVENTORY'S WIDTH: the critic's target of 24.9% of frame is ~805x641 at 4:3-ish, and `COLS` in `screens/inventory.js` needs 200+20+132+24+640+30 = 1046 units of WIDTH for its four columns before the detail panel gets any. So the inventory specifically cannot reach 24.9% by shrinking alone; it needs its columns re-pitched. The other four screens (journal 0.1315, level-up 0.0911, sheet 0.0896, spells 0.0703) are where a contents-sized box is genuinely cheap. I did NOT pad a number and I did not add decorative fill.

I PROCEEDED PAST A `node tools/contention.mjs` WAIT ONCE, and it is recorded here rather than left for someone to find. The second probe run (the one that verified the journal fix) was launched in a shell that ran `contention.mjs` and the probe with `;` rather than `&&`; contention printed `WAIT — the box is at or over its ceiling` and the probe ran anyway. It completed cleanly and its numbers agree with the two runs either side of it. Every other browser run in this piece was launched behind a GO.

THE AXIS REPEAT STILL CANNOT FIRE ON A PAUSED SCREEN, ON ANY DEVICE, AND I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX IT. Measured in my own passing evidence: TS1's held touch drag moved `focus.inventory.rowIdx` from 2 to 3 — EXACTLY ONE ROW — over 12 fixed steps. The cause is `UISystem._edge()` at `game/src/ui/system.js:566`, which gates the repeat on `held = frame - axis.since` against `REPEAT_FIRST = 14`; on a paused screen `ctx.frame` is `sim.frame` and does not advance, so `held` is always 0 and the repeat is unreachable. This is device-NEUTRAL — holding a direction on the keyboard on a paused screen moves one row too — so it is not a touch-arm fail and OP3's 'a list you can open and cannot walk' is now satisfied (it walks, one flick per row). THE REMEDY IS KNOWN AND I REFUSED IT ON A MEASURED RISK, not on a feeling: a monotonic UI tick (`sim.frame + uiPausedFrames`, both already live in `engine.js`) passed only to `_edge`. `REPEAT_FIRST` is 14 and SEVERAL SHIPPED PROBES HOLD KEYS FOR EXACTLY 14 FRAMES — `tools/ui/t4-r2-critic-focus.mjs`'s own `key(code, 14)` in the fifteen-action exit walk is one — so that change silently turns a one-row move into a two-row move underneath the instruments this piece is judged with. It needs its own piece with those probes re-run, not a line at the end of this one.

I DID NOT PHOTOGRAPH ANY OF IT. Everything here is driven state and element census through real DOM events; there is no PNG in my artifacts and I ran no `tools/visual/frame-liveness.mjs`, because I measured no frame. That is honest for what these three defects are — a trapped view, a silent control and a dead axis are all invisible in a still, which is `RI-UIX10`'s own opening argument — but it means the ONE thing I built that is a drawn thing rather than a state change, the in-combat 'Putting it on' line and its progress rule in `screens/inventory.js` `detail()`, IS DECLARED AND UNPHOTOGRAPHED. It is asserted in the element census (`detail_panel.meta.equipping`, `list_row.meta.equipping`, and the `inventory.hint` text) and it is NOT proven to be legible pixels. Score that arm 0 fail-closed if it matters to you; the capture that would settle it is an in-combat inventory shot 15 frames after a confirm on a weapon row.

RI-UIX10 OP2 (gamepad) WAS NOT RE-RUN BY ME. My paused-frame fix touches the shared input tick, so the pad arm deserves a re-run and got one only indirectly, through `t4-r2-critic-drive.mjs`. The pad's own path is unaffected by construction — `RealInput.pollGamepad()` runs from rAF and delivers EDGES into `pendingPress`, which `latchForStep()` picks up without any per-step poll — but 'unaffected by construction' is an argument and not a measurement.

HUD1 IN MY EVIDENCE IS RED IN ALL THREE RUNS AND IT IS NOT A DEFECT. `two_hand` reports dead at 8/13, 10/13 and 12/13 alike. It is `RI-UIX10` trap I2 — a gated hold cannot cross on a paused screen in a harness because `hold-gate.js inputNow()` returns `frame * STEP_MS` and the frame is frozen. The brief warned me about exactly this and it is the first thing I checked. My paused-frame fix does NOT disarm it and was not meant to: what is frozen is the clock, not the poll.

2_equip_is_silent_out_of_combat.the_seam_question_the_brief_asked_me_to_: RI-UIX03 P7's PROPERTY TEXT is unconditional — 'changing an equipped weapon or armour piece costs an animation-committed action of >= 30 frames during which the player is vulnerable' — but ITS OWN COMPARISON METHOD IS NOT. Comparison-method step 5 reads 'Equip a different weapon from the menu DURING COMBAT; assert the trace shows a committed state of >=30 frames with iframe:false', and M-P5 is scored on that run and only that run. So the item states the property unconditionally and measures it conditionally, and the out-of-combat case is genuinely unaddressed. THAT IS THE FINDING. I ruled it rather than asking: CLAUDE.md settles it — 'Souls wins INSIDE the fight; Morrowind wins everywhere else' — and out of combat there is no fight, no frame in which 'during which the player is vulnerable' can be true (RI-UIX03 P1 stops the world, measured at frame delta 0 of 120), and RI-UIX10's own bar cites Morrowind's inventory by name: 'the moment you equip something the figure in the corner is wearing it'. A 30-frame cost taken out of a stopped clock is not a cost, it is a hang. REVERSIBLE, and the evidence that would overturn it is written into the code comment: an amendment to P7 that states the commitment out of combat AND names what the player is vulnerable to on a stopped clock, or an item requiring a wind-down animation on the world body when a menu closes.

3_touch_stick_never_reaches_the_pipeline.cause_found_not_guessed: THE PAUSED BRANCH OF `Engine._step()` RETURNS BEFORE `stepOnce()`, AND `stepOnce()` IS THE ONLY CALLER OF `sim.realInput.tick(sim.frame)` (`game/src/sim/step.js:90`). `RealInput.tick()` calling `TouchInput.tick()` is the only place the floating stick is pushed into the pipeline — `touch.js` `tick()`: `if (this.stick.active) ... this.pipe.setMove(...)`. A finger holds a POSITION; something has to read that position once per step, and on a paused frame nothing did. Out of combat every screen pauses (RI-UIX03 P1, working as designed), so the stick was dead on every screen and live nowhere the screens are. Keyboard and pad were unaffected and that is why it survived two rounds: both deliver EDGES into `pendingPress`, which `latchForStep()` picks up with no per-step poll. Only touch feeds the analogue channel while a screen is open.
3_touch_stick_never_reaches_the_pipeline.change: game/src/engine.js `_step()` paused branch — `if (this.sim.realInput) this.sim.realInput.tick(this.sim.frame);` before `latchForStep`, the same call with the same argument `stepOnce()` makes. Idempotent on a frame that does not advance, and in mode `play` both hold pollers are skipped inside it anyway (`RealInput.tick`'s `modeOf() !== 'play'` guard and `TouchInput.playClock`), so it does not disarm trap I2.
